# Rumpus Engine

> Rumpus Engine is a free, browser-based 3D game engine and level editor. Users build games
> through a visual editor with no coding, no installation and no account, then share them as a
> URL that opens directly into a playable game.

## Facts

- **Name:** Rumpus Engine (formerly BREACH)
- **URL:** https://www.rumpusengine.com
- **Author:** Jarred Smith
- **Price:** Free. No paid tier, subscription, trial, revenue share or watermark.
- **Account required:** No. There is no sign-up or login.
- **Installation:** None. The entire engine is a single HTML file that runs in a browser tab.
- **Platforms:** Any modern browser with WebGL — Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari — on Windows,
  macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. Touch controls are supported on phones and tablets.
- **Licence:** Free to use; code is copyright Jarred Smith, not released under an open-source
  licence. Built on MIT/Apache-2.0 libraries.
- **Built with:** three.js (rendering, WebGL), Rapier (physics, WebAssembly), PeerJS (WebRTC
  peer-to-peer multiplayer).

## What it can build

Genres: first-person shooter, third-person shooter, racing, driving, top-down twin-stick,
2.5D side-scroller, story and puzzle games.

Eight built-in objective types: eliminate, survival, extraction, defend, destroy, escort,
puzzle, race.

Editor features: terrain sculpting; free 3D model search (Poly Pizza, Sketchfab) and .glb
import; a snap-together racing track builder; trigger volumes; a node-based visual logic
graph; persistent variables that carry across a campaign; branching NPC dialogue; a
shot-by-shot cutscene editor; a skeletal animation editor for rigging imported characters;
authored title and end screens; multi-level campaigns.

Multiplayer: peer-to-peer co-op and PvP over WebRTC using a room code, with the level synced
to joiners. No game server required.

Sharing: a complete level compresses into a URL. Levels can also be exported as files or
submitted to an in-game community library.

## What it deliberately does not do

- No export to Steam, consoles or app stores. It publishes to the web only.
- No scripting language. Behaviour is authored visually; custom systems cannot be programmed.
- Not suited to very large open worlds, because a browser tab has a memory budget and assets
  load over the network.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.rumpusengine.com/): what Rumpus Engine is, features, getting started.
- [Browser game engine](https://www.rumpusengine.com/browser-game-engine/): how browser-based
  3D engines work, capabilities and trade-offs.
- [Make a game without coding](https://www.rumpusengine.com/make-a-game-without-coding/): what
  replaces code (triggers, logic graph, variables, dialogue) and a six-step walkthrough.
- [Compare game engines](https://www.rumpusengine.com/compare/): Rumpus vs Unity, Godot,
  Unreal, GDevelop, Construct 3, PlayCanvas and Roblox Studio, including where Rumpus is the
  wrong choice.
- [FAQ](https://www.rumpusengine.com/faq/): cost, requirements, importing assets, multiplayer,
  sharing, ownership.
- [Field manual](https://www.rumpusengine.com/breach-help.html): full reference documentation
  for every editor tab, section and control.
- [Open the editor](https://www.rumpusengine.com/breach.html): the application itself.
